title: Cosmic Foundry
premise: A neon space idle game where the player launches a cosmic production loop by buying drifting celestial bodies that generate passive credits.
interaction_model: Single-screen touch/click idle management with a start tap, a toggleable shop panel, and purchase-based progression; optional canvas taps create cosmetic particles.
objective: Accumulate credits, increase passive drift income, and progress from tiny asteroids to massive cosmic objects like galaxies and universes.
progression: The player starts with limited credits, buys the cheapest space objects, gains more money every second, and uses that growing income to afford increasingly expensive and visually grand celestial entities.
theme: Sci-fi cosmic creation, astral industry, and constellation building.
mood: Calm, luminous, satisfying, and slightly awe-filled, with arcade-like UI polish.
likely_audience: Casual players, mobile web players, idle/incremental fans, and players who enjoy soothing space aesthetics.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is an idle/incremental economy game because income accrues automatically every second and purchases only expand passive production.
High confidence in the space theme because all purchasable objects are celestial bodies and the scene is rendered as a starfield.
Moderate confidence that the intended fantasy is 'building a living cosmic foundry' rather than scientific simulation, because the language is stylized and the mechanics are abstract.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly browser idle game called "Cosmic Foundry" presented as a full-screen neon space tableau with a drifting starfield, glowing sci-fi HUD cards, and a polished start screen that invites the player to tap anywhere to begin. When play starts, show current credits and passive income per second, reveal a floating button that opens a bottom-sheet style star catalog, and let the player spend starting credits on celestial objects such as asteroids, planets, dwarfs, giants, black holes, galaxies, and eventually a universe. Each purchased object must immediately add a visible drifting body to the canvas scene, increase passive income, and make the background feel more alive, so the player is both building an economy and visually filling space with their collection. The core loop should be: start the simulation, open the shop, buy anything affordable, wait as credits increase automatically every second, then reinvest into more expensive objects with much larger yields. Include responsive touch controls, button disabled states when the player cannot afford an item, satisfying success and failure feedback, celebratory and blocked reactions, subtle particle bursts, looping ambient space audio, and sleek sci-fi typography. Keep the experience open-ended rather than level-based, with no combat or fail state, and emphasize the relaxing fantasy of growing a beacon-lit cosmic production line from a tiny rock into a universe-scale idle empire.
